items.title: Lam Research Soars 9% on $25 Billion Buyback as Chip Stocks Rebound From Rout
items.summary: Key TakeawaysLam Research shares jumped 9% today after its board approved a $25 billion buyback, outpacing ASML and the other chip-equipment makers in the rebound. Lam had no other news, so the buyback is the clearest reason for the extra gain, and it’s a strong vote of confidence.

items.title: SanDisk Surges 10%, Micron and Western Digital Jump 8% as Memory and Storage Stocks Rebound From AI Sell-Off
items.summary: Chip stocks just survived one of their ugliest sessions in years, and the trigger was politics, not earnings. Why are memory bulls still cautious, and which new threat could send the selloff roaring back?

items.title: Chip Stocks Just Had Their Second-Worst Day on Record
items.summary: Chip stocks erased roughly $1.5 trillion in a single session, and nobody agrees on why. Regulation fears, hedge fund profit-taking, and a capex slowdown all compete for blame, and the real culprit decides what happens next.

items.title: AI semiconductor rout may be buying opportunity, LYNX Equity says: ’Dip a toe in’
items.summary: Investing.com -- Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) shares rebounded sharply in premarket trading Friday after the semiconductor equipment maker announced a $25 billion share repurchase authorization, offering a potential signal of corporate confidence following one of the technology sector’s worst trading sessions in years.

items.title: Lam Research Sure Picked a Good Time to Buy Back Its Own Stock
items.summary: The chip tool maker is leading the way in the AI rebound after its board greenlit a $25 billion stock buyback program.
